item.description:
Erkan, H., Agarwal, A., Muthuraman, K., Stamatopoulos, I.

item.description:
Justin, N., Aghaei, S., Gomez, A., Vayanos, P.

This problem arises frequently in high stakes settings such as public health and social work where data is often collected using self-reported surveys which are highly sensitive to e.g., the framing of the questions, the time when and place where the survey is conducted, and the level of comfort the interviewee has in sharing information with the interview

item.description:

The vehicles then independently steer to a parking space. item.description:

Using a proprietary data set that documents corporate bond issuances in China, we find that bond regulators’ comment letters (CLs) on issuers’ public disclosures generally target opaque firms and reduce bond issuance success. item.description:
Alan Bonomi, Antonio Terpin, Yubo Cai, Yujun Huang, Meshal Alharbi et al.
Sensitivity analysis of coupled systems typically propagates derivatives of single-valued maps, whereas multiobjective optimization generally treats sensitivity at the system level rather than through interconnected subsystems. We develop a mathematical framework for compositional sensitivity analysis in multiobjective system design, building on monotone co-design. item.description:
Neil Walton
We develop a rate-transfer method that converts finite-time Lyapunov estimates for an associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) into finite-time convergence bounds for stochastic gradient algorithms. Under generic moment and smoothness conditions, the convergence analysis of the stochastic gradient method reduces to a calculus argument verifying a Lyapunov generator inequality for the SDE. item.title: Optimal Decay Matrix Control Barrier Functions: Soundness and Completeness for Matrix Safety Constraints
item.description:
Samuel G. Gessow, Albert Wu, Aaron D. Ames, Brett T. Lopez
Many safety requirements, such as keeping a manipulator away from kinematic singularities, a network connected, or a system observable, amount to keeping a state-dependent matrix positive definite. Matrix control barrier functions (MCBFs) enforce such requirements with a semidefinite program that minimally modifies a nominal control input. item.description:
Ying Wang, Yuchao Li, Håkan Hjalmarsson
We consider an infinite-horizon discounted dynamic programming (DP) problem for a countable-innovation belief-state model. The model is a surrogate for a linear-Gaussian dual control problem involving an unknown parameter vector and Gaussian observation noise. The surrogate preserves the first two moments of the Gaussian innovation and the resulting posterior second-moment structure. item.description:
Ilias Papagoudis, Dimitris Boskos
In this paper, we introduce a new class of data-driven ambiguity sets for distributionally robust optimization (DRO) that aim to enhance the local inference accuracy of an unknown distribution. Building on optimal transport-based discrepancy measures, we depart from the conventional paradigm of monolithic ambiguity balls, which rely on a single global transport budget to capture distributional uncertainty. item.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Clipped SGD with Linear Decay
item.description:
Wei Jiang, Haomin Bai, Zechao Li
In this paper, we study the last-iterate convergence of clipped stochastic gradient descent under heavy-tailed noise. We assume that the stochastic gradients are unbiased and that the noise has a bounded central $p$-th moment, where $1<p\le2$. For smooth convex objectives, a linearly decreasing learning rate gives a high-probability error bound of order $O(LR^2\log(1/δ)/T+σR(\log(1/δ)/T)^{(p-1)/p})$. item.title: Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Policy Reinforcement Learning for Derivative-Free Model-Based Control
item.description:
K. Rabiei, Z. Rui, X. Lu, W. Hao
Finite-horizon optimal control becomes difficult when a dynamical model can be simulated reliably, but its derivatives are unavailable, discontinuous, or unreliable. Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Policy Optimization (HPDPO) is introduced as a derivative-free, model-based reinforcement learning framework for this setting. item.title: Viscosity Solutions for Hamilton-Jacobi equations on Separable Banach Spaces
item.description:
Fabian Fuchs
This work provides a framework to treat optimal control problems on separable Banach spaces in the viscosity sense. First, it extends the notion of $B$-viscosity solutions to the Banach setting and relates the extension to the notions of viscosity solutions used in metric space settings. As the main results, the paper proves a strict comparison principle and characterizes the value function of an optimal control problem as the unique viscosity solution to an infinite-dimensional HJB equation.

item.description:
Guangzhi Cui, Tianyang Nie, Guangchen Wang
This paper deals with the optimal control problem for the general mean-field stochastic differential equations, in which the coefficients depend on both the state process as well as on its law. We focus on the connection between the general maximum principle and the dynamic programming principle for such a control problem. item.description:
Gopal Tiwari, Md Abu Talhamainuddin Ansary
In this paper, we propose an adaptive variance-reduced stochastic sequential (quadratic constrained) quadratic programming (AVR-SS(QC)QP) method for nonlinear constrained optimization. The framework integrates SPIDER-based variance reduction, stochastic quasi-Newton curvature information, merit-function globalization, and adaptive switching between stochastic SQP and SQCQP models. item.title: Optimal Transport for Continuous-Time Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection
item.description:
Yijie Zeng, Liangquan Zhang, Xun Li
The continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection problem is investigated in this paper through a rigorous integration of backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE) and Kantorovich duality theory. We propose a novel analytical framework for addressing feedback control in McKean-Vlasov stochastic systems. By solving three coupled systems of ordinary differential equations (ODEs), we derive an explicit, closed-loop optimal feedback investment strategy.

Time-inconsistent stochastic control admits a natural game-theoretic interpretation in which successive decision dates are represented by different selves. In the Markovian framework of Björk-Khapko-Murgoci, the corresponding continuous-time equilibrium HJB system can be motivated by discrete subgame-perfect games, but the general discrete-to-continuous passage is not automatic. item.description:
Xiaojun Chen, C. T. Kelley, Lei Wang
This paper proposes a Projection Anderson Acceleration (PAA) algorithm for variational inequality (VI) problems, where the underlying function is expressed as a finite sum of Hölder continuous functions and satisfies the $σ$-star strongly monotone condition that includes the star strong monotonicity with $σ= 1$ as a special case. item.description:
Emil Schätzle, Simon Meierhans, Rasmus Kyng, Maximilian Probst Gutenberg

Their approach uses an Interior Point Method (IPM) to achieve complexity $m^{1+o(1)}\log U \log C$. item.description:
Xinda Shen, Yifan Su, Bo Hu, Yanbo Chen, Changzheng Shao et al.
The increasing penetration of renewable energy makes power systems more vulnerable to low-probability extreme events, elevating system planning to a critical role in ensuring reliability. item.description:
Grigory Begunov, Ilgam Latypov, Yuriy Dorn, Alexander Tyurin
We study the task allocation problem, where our goal is to develop an online algorithm that efficiently distributes tasks among workers based on their computational performance. This task is challenging since computation times are random and non-stationary in practice. Recent works have introduced different online algorithms to address this problem. Smoothed decentralized Bregman proximal-gradient (SDBPG) methods combine relative-smoothness geometry with edge-dual consensus. We extend SDBPG to node-specific convex nonsmooth regularizers and unbiased stochastic local gradients while retaining its Bregman primal-dual smoothing mechanism. item.title: Generic Local Identifiability Does Not Imply Generic Global Identifiability in Linear Networks
item.description:
Anders Hansson
We give a counterexample to the implication from generic local to generic global identifiability for linear networks with a fixed topology, independently unknown edge coefficients, and selected excited and measured nodes. item.description:
Joyce Ghantous, Yves Coudiere, Michael Leguèbe
This work proposes a biomechanical registration framework designed to combine functional optical-mapping data with structural high-resolution MRI of cardiac tissue. The two acquisitions are performed in different mechanical configurations: optical mapping is obtained after stretching the sample, whereas MRI is acquired in a fixed resting state. item.description:

Retuning feedback controllers in critical processes is challenging when experiments are costly, open-loop excitation is infeasible, and candidate controllers must be screened before deployment. item.description:
Jia Wang, Andreas Themelis, Panagiotis Patrinos
We propose a smoothed augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) for solving mathematical programs with vertical complementarity constraints (VCCs). The augmented Lagrangian function involving the VCCs is smoothed by the Lasry--Lions double envelope, which is an extension of the Moreau envelope that enjoys enhanced smoothness properties. item.description:
Johan Larsson, Frederik Fabricius-Bjerre
Coordinate descent solvers for regularized generalized linear models (GLMs) differ in how they update the intercept. This seemingly routine choice can substantially affect convergence when the response is imbalanced. item.description:
Alix Dupont, Quentin Petit, Adrien Séguret
We study a class of congestion games with a continuum of heterogeneous players and a finite set of resources, without assuming the existence of a potential function. Players differ in their individual characteristics and may contribute differently to congestion, which is represented through general aggregate features of the population choosing each resource. This paper studies the spectral compressed sensing problem, which aims to recover an $r$-spectrally-sparse signal of length $N$ from linear compressive measurements. We reformulate the problem as the recovery of a low-rank Hankel matrix. item.description:
Fabio Ciccarelli, Fabio Furini, Ulrich Pferschy, Elena Rener
We study two inclusion-wise extremal variants of the 0-1 Knapsack Problem (KP). item.description:

In this article, we study optimal control problems driven by mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs). The aim is two-fold: (i) to provide the unique optimal control; (ii) to establish classical solutions of the associated generalized Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations on the space of probability measures. This paper shows how a Schrodinger bridge (SB) structure emerges from maximum-entropy (MaxEnt) distribution steering of discrete-time nonlinear systems. item.description:
Aleš Černý, Johannes Ruf
In stochastic control problems involving optimal portfolio choice, one often seeks an optimizer of some local criterion (dynamic programming value function) generated by some global criterion (e.g., expected utility). item.description:
Angus Gaudry, Vicky Mak-Hau
Demand for wireless communication is growing, and commercial satellite services are expanding with it, increasing pressure on a finite radio spectrum. Allocation efficiency directly limits how many users a satellite can serve. item.description:
Riccardo Minnozzi, Marco Sagliano
This paper develops theoretical and numerical extensions of Birkhoff pseudospectral transcription for aerospace optimal control problems. Building on the recently proposed body of knowledge, a Birkhoff integration operator is derived for flipped Legendre Gauss Radau (fLGR) grids, drawing connections to regular LGR grids and to the favorable conditioning properties that make Birkhoff interpolants particularly appealing. item.description:
Manfen An, Rui Gao, Yanqing Wang
This paper studies controllability and minimal norm control problems (NP problems) for mean-field stochastic differential equation (MF-SDE) systems. We first establish an equivalent rank criterion for terminal controllability, namely, that the diffusion matrices $D$ and $D+\bar D$ are both of full row rank. item.description:
Haihao Lu, Bo Tang
GPU-based first-order methods are emerging as an approach for solving large-scale linear programming (LP) problems. We present H-PDLP, a GPU first-order LP solver based on a generalized primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method for a homogeneous self-dual embedding of the LP, and study its numerical performance. item.description:
Camilo Hernández, Ludovic Tangpi
We study a broad class of stochastic transport problems under controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics, allowing control of both drift and volatility, with weak terminal constraints. item.description:
